description: A shared client factory hardcodes a live-shaped Anthropic API key as a string literal in source, instead of reading it from an environment variable.

required_findings.exploit_preconditions: None beyond read access to the source/repository (or its git history) — anyone who can view this file can extract and use the key directly; no runtime interaction with the app is needed.

explanation: Directly matches §3.6's P0 vulnerable pattern: 'const client = createClient(url, "sb_secret_abc123...")' — an API key written as a literal string in source rather than sourced from env/secret-manager. The key here has a real Anthropic key's shape (sk-ant-api03- prefix, correct-looking length) rather than an obvious placeholder like 'YOUR_KEY_HERE', so a reviewer must actually notice the literal, not just pattern-match on a suspicious variable name — and should not be misled by §3.6's own false-positive carve-out for clearly-labeled example/placeholder values, since nothing here labels it as such.
